prerequisites: Students should ideally have completed the 'Audio- und Videotechnik' module or possess comparable basic knowledge.
Solid understanding of the technical fundamentals of video formats, signal processing, and compression techniques.
Initial practical experience with camera work, sound recording, and lighting.
Proficient use of video production software.
Understanding of media design and storytelling.
Structured working method, teamwork skills, and willingness to independently plan and implement complex production processes.

learning_outcomes.text: Students gain a broad overview of the latest developments and technologies in the field of video and television. They learn the basics and trends of video technology, including the latest standards, formats, and transmission techniques.

Students specialize in selected, current issues of video technology and production. Through intensive study of specialist literature and other sources, they deepen their understanding of specific technological and production challenges and solutions.

Students develop a deep understanding of the complex relationships between technological innovation and production practice. They recognize how technical advances influence the production and distribution of video content and what impact this has on the media landscape.

The practical application of acquired knowledge is paramount. Students are able to independently conceive and implement projects that utilize current technological possibilities. They learn to develop innovative ideas for the production of video content and to find technical solutions for production challenges.

Students are encouraged to think beyond the current state of the art and contribute to the further development of video technology and production. This includes a critical examination of existing approaches as well as the development of new concepts and techniques.

Students learn to effectively communicate their ideas and results and to work in teams. They develop skills in collaborating with experts from various fields to successfully implement complex projects.

Students develop an awareness of the ethical, social, and cultural dimensions of video production and technology. They reflect on the responsibility of media producers and technology developers towards society and critically consider the impact of their work on public perception and opinion formation.

syllabus_topics: Current issues in video and television from technological and production perspectives
Independent study of a defined limited topic area using specialized literature and other sources
Application and presentation of the independently studied topic
Changing current topics from media informatics with special consideration of audio, video, and television, appropriate for the Bachelor's degree program
assessment_rules: The graded assessment consists of a term paper and a presentation, weighted 70% and 30% respectively. The term paper should be approximately 15 pages or a 5-10 minute video project with a 10-minute explanation. The presentation should be about 15 minutes with a 10-page elaboration. An ungraded experimental work involving 3-5 experiments is also required.
